newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovaks mull sale of stake in Czech KB.
newsitem.headline: Slovaks mull sale of stake in Czech KB.

text.p: The Slovak National Property Fund (NPF) said on Tuesday it was preparing negotiations with an unspecified Asian financial investor over the sale of its stake in Czech bank Komercni Banka a.s.

"We are pepared to open talks in the near future with a strong financial investor from Asia which has shown eminent interest in purchasing the Slovak stake in the Czech Komercni Banka," the fund said in a statement.
The statement did not give further details, saying no additional information would be made public until the transaction was completed. NPF officials were not available for further comment.

The Czech and Slovak Republics, which were created out of the Czechoslovak federation in 1993, agreed to split former state assets under a formula giving Prague two thirds and Bratislava one third of the property.
Under the agreement, the Slovak NPF obtained about a 15 percent stake in Komercni Banka which is the largest Czech commercial bank.
The Czech NPF also holds around 33 percent in the largest Slovak commercial bank VUB a.s..
However, neither of the two privatisation funds can execute their shareholders' rights in banks of the other country.
Shares of Komercni Banka belonging to the Slovak NPF are registered on the Czech NPF account in Prague.

The Czech state retains partial control over its four largest banks -- IPB, Komercni Banka, Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka and the largest savings bank Ceska Sporitelna, through stakes held by the Czech NPF.
